title: Linguistic Analysis of Diagnostic Interviews with Young Patients
summary: Since the 1990s, the Department of Language and Communication at the University of Bielefeld has been analyzing doctor-patient encounters with the aim of finding out how talking about seizures in patients with epileptic seizures differs from the way patients with non-epileptic seizures talk about their seizures. It could be shown that the tools of linguistics are suitable for making the correct classification in adult patients. The study aims to clarify how children and adolescents differ from adult patients in the way they report epileptic and non-epileptic seizure events.

interventions.name: In our clinic children and adolescents who present with seizures of unknown etiology are supposed to talk to the doctor alone, if they have the courage and the ability to do so. If parents and patient agree, this encounter is recorded. The recording is then transcribed at the Fakultät für Linguistik

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patient is presenting in the hospital because of paroxsymal events
Exclusion criteria:
Patients must be able and willing to speak to the doctor alone
